subject: [PATCH v2 10/12] mm/collapse: work out the orders a VMA allows once per VMA

2026-09-10.patch_summary: This patch optimizes the way possible memory orders are determined for a VMA (Virtual Memory Area) by calculating them once per VMA instead of once per PTE table. This is done to reduce unnecessary work and improve performance. The patch also ensures that changes to hugepage enablement take effect after one VMA has been processed, preventing widening of collapses.

reviews.author: Zi Yan
reviews.summary: Identified the need for a more efficient approach to calculating allowed orders per VMA, but did not provide further technical comments or suggestions.
reviews.raw_body:
On Thu Sep 10, 2026 at 8:02 AM EDT, Kiryl Shutsemau wrote:
> From: "Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta)" <kas@kernel.org>
>
> The scan asked collapse_possible_orders() for every PTE table, for an
> answer that is a property of the VMA.  Both callers walk a VMA a table at
> a time, so let them work it out once and pass the mask in.  It is only
> good while the lock that produced it is held, so madvise_collapse() takes
> it again after every collapse.
>
> The mask is then sampled once per VMA rather than once per table.  A thp
> enabled knob written during a walk takes effect one VMA later, and cannot
> widen a collapse: hugepage_vma_revalidate() tests the order again under
> the lock the collapse retakes.
>
> Assisted-by: LLM
> Signed-off-by: Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta) <kas@kernel.org>
> ---
>  mm/khugepaged.c | 32 ++++++++++++++++++--------------
>  1 file changed, 18 insertions(+), 14 deletions(-)
>
LGTM.

Reviewed-by: Zi Yan <ziy@nvidia.com>


-- 
Best Regards,
Yan, Zi

2026-09-11.patch_summary: This patch series aims to optimize the collapse functionality in the Linux kernel by allowing VMA (Virtual Memory Area) to work out the allowed orders once per VMA, reducing unnecessary computations and improving performance.
